sources.entry: bknd | Lightweight Firebase/Supabase alternative with database, auth, media and an admin UI

summary.one_liner: bknd is a lightweight, web-standards-based visual backend offering database, authentication, media and workflow primitives with an integrated admin UI, positioned as an alternative to Firebase or Supabase.
summary.what_it_does: bknd provides a REST API covering data (entities that can be defined, queried and controlled), auth, media file management and flows (workflows, with UI integration described as coming soon). It is built on the WinterTC Minimum Common Web Platform APIs and is meant to run in many JavaScript runtimes, including Node.js, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Netlify and AWS Lambda, or inside a framework such as Next.js, React Router or Astro. The package includes an admin UI for managing data and configuration, a TypeScript SDK with React hooks, and React components for auth forms and media upload. The README also mentions a built-in MCP server and client. Database options named include SQLite variants (LibSQL, Cloudflare D1, Bun SQLite) and Postgres (Supabase, Neon, Xata), and storage options include S3-compatible services, Cloudinary and the filesystem.
use_cases: Headless CMS or WordPress-style content site
Backend for AI agent state persistence
Multi-tenant SaaS backend with user management
Type-safe REST API backend with OpenAPI
Small-footprint backend for IoT or embedded devices
notable: Runs on many runtimes and edge platforms from one codebase, built on Web Standards
Modular, opt-in data, auth, media and flows components
Adapter-based infrastructure with direct access to underlying drivers
Built-in admin UI, TypeScript SDK, React hooks and React auth/media elements
Built-in MCP server, client and UI
caveats: Requires Node.js 22.13 or higher for the node:sqlite dependency
Under active development; backward compatibility not guaranteed before v1.0.0
Flows UI integration is marked as coming soon
